record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: How can the homogenized equations for a mixture of elastic solid and compressible viscous fluid be extended from small linearized vibrations to the general motion of the mixture with large deformations?

status_evidence.title: Homogenization of large deforming fluid-saturated porous structures
status_evidence.snippet: Two-scale computational homogenization method proposed for modelling of locally periodic fluid-saturated media subjected to large deformation induced by quasistatic loading.
status_evidence.claim: Computational homogenization frameworks for large-deformation fluid-saturated porous media have been proposed, but a fully rigorous theory covering the general dynamic case with compressible viscous fluid remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Homogenization of a mixture of elastic solids and a slightly viscous fluid
status_evidence.snippet: Two-scale convergence method to derive effective equations with Darcy's law for three-phase structures in the linearized vibration regime.
status_evidence.claim: Linearized small-vibration homogenization of solid-fluid mixtures is well established.

artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous two-scale homogenization is well developed for small linearized vibrations (Biot/Darcy-type effective equations). For the fully nonlinear large-deformation regime with compressible viscous fluid, only partial results exist: computational/formal two-scale schemes for quasistatic large deformations of fluid-saturated porous media have been proposed, but a complete rigorous derivation including dynamics and moving interfaces is not established. The problem is best regarded as partially solved / largely open.
